posts.title: Van Allen’s Doughnuts: A Radiation Belt Retrospective
posts.description: In 1958, a physicist launched a satellite and discovered Earth is surrounded by invisible doughnut-shaped rings of trapped radiation. Nobody had thought to check before. The universe had been running this infrastructure for billions of years without filing a disclosure notice.

posts.title: Planets We Were Fairly Sure About Until We Weren’t: A Retrospective
posts.description: Science revises itself. That's not a bug — it's the entire point. A brief history of planetary confidence, and the moments the universe quietly suggested we have another look.

posts.title: Gravitons: Delulu but Make It Theoretical
posts.description: Gravity has been the main character of the universe for 13.8 billion years and still hasn't confirmed its own carrier particle. A deep dive into the most wanted, most elusive, and most theoretically inevitable particle in all of physics — and the extraordinary experiments trying to catch one.
